column1: # What works where – read by the website and the README. yes = tested on that system · partial = works with the limit in the note · built = the code is there, not yet tested on that system · soon = being built · no = not possible there

column5: note
Windows: PowerShell 7 and Windows Terminal; the same settings file and logos.

column1: Slash commands and your own shortcuts
column5: In bash the typed line is rewritten, so you see the real command. Windows: PowerShell's Enter key (PSReadLine) rewrites the line – the rewriting is tested, the key in a real window not yet.
Windows: they think with /ai (Claude, Ollama, OpenAI-compatible).
macOS: caffeinate · Linux: systemd-inhibit. Windows: SetThreadExecutionState

column1: AI terminal and web chat (Claude, Ollama, any OpenAI-compatible API)
column5: On Linux the AI program is one downloaded file checked against a pinned digest, or built when the Swift toolchain is installed. Apple Intelligence is macOS only. Windows: /ai chats and answers (also explain, write, summarize, command), without tools – the AI terminal and the web chat are not on Windows yet.

column1: A local model that Lotus runs (MLX)
column5: Apple silicon only. Elsewhere use Ollama or llama.cpp: /ai talks to both.

column1: The AI looks at the web pages it builds
column5: Linux needs Chromium, Chrome or Edge.
macOS: Apple ImageIO · Linux: ImageMagick. Windows: ImageMagick from winget – tested on x64; the Arm64 test machine has no ImageMagick that works.
Windows: x64 only – PyTorch has no build for Windows on Arm; on the processor, without the drawing editor. Tested on GitHub's Windows machine: the runtime, BiRefNet Lite and a real cut-out.
yt-dlp and ffmpeg. Windows: yt-dlp and ffmpeg from winget – the download is tested with stand-ins on Linux, not yet on Windows.
Windows: this PC only – the phones in the Wi-Fi and the QR code not yet. Python 3.9 or newer.
Macs (lotus meshchat) and Windows 10 2004 or 11 (meshchat.exe) chat together over Bluetooth LE. The same protocol, checked byte for byte on both on every change; not yet tried between real computers.
Java 17 or newer; Lotus can fetch one with a checksum. Windows: tested with a real Paper server on GitHub's Windows machine; a server started in its own window (start.cmd) is stopped there.
Limited plugins run in a sandbox (macOS: sandbox-exec · Linux: bubblewrap). Without one they are refused, never run unprotected.

column1: Now playing line and album cover
column5: Linux: over MPRIS (playerctl), tested with a stand-in player. Windows: the line, from Windows' media controls through fastfetch; no album cover yet.
Linux: playerctl. Windows: the media keys and the volume of Core Audio – the volume is tested on Windows, the keys and the visualizer not yet.
Linux: the desktop entries of your system, Flatpak and Snap. Windows: the apps of the Start menu – finding them by name is tested, opening one in a real session not yet.
Linux: your package manager, the exact command first and a question before anything is installed. Windows: winget – every id of the catalog is checked against winget on every change.
Windows: install.ps1, lotus.cmd in your user PATH, the profile block; lotus uninstall takes it all out.
Linux: built, not yet tested. Windows: built, not yet tested.
Needs Apple tools.
